original_question: Given a sequence (alpha_n)_{n>=1} with 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0, give a recursive descriptive formula for the Cantor set obtained by the variable-gap middle-interval construction in which the open middle interval removed at stage n has length alpha_n.
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper's intended target very closely. It correctly identifies the variable-gap middle-interval construction, keeps the two hypotheses stated in the paper for the sequence (alpha_n), and asks for a recursive descriptive formula rather than a broader classification or an explicit closed-form formula.
missing_details: The paper works with deterministic Cantor sets on the real line, concretely as subsets of the unit interval [0,1], so the ambient space should be stated explicitly.

At stage n, one does not remove a single interval globally; one removes the open middle subinterval of length alpha_n from each surviving closed interval present after stage n-1, so there are 2^{n-1} deletions at stage n.

To make the question stand alone, the recursive construction should introduce the stage sets explicitly, e.g. C_0 = [0,1], C_n obtained from C_{n-1} by the prescribed deletions, and C = intersection_{n>=0} C_n.

The paper's notion of a recursive descriptive formula is set-theoretic/nested in flavor, so it is helpful to ask for a recursive nested description of the limit set, not merely a prose description of the deletion algorithm.

The sum condition should be understood as the feasibility condition ensuring that the total removed length does not exceed 1; equivalently, each stage-n middle gap must fit inside every surviving interval at stage n-1.

The problem should remain in the symmetric middle-deletion setting. The paper separates the question of relaxing or enforcing symmetry into the distinct open problem (iv), so that issue should not be folded into the present question.

The question should stay narrowly about finding a recursive description of the resulting Cantor set, not about proving extra properties such as Hausdorff dimension, measure, or IFS realizability unless those are explicitly requested.
refined_question: Let (alpha_n)_{n>=1} be a fixed sequence in (0,1) such that 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0. Starting from C_0 = [0,1], define recursively for each n>=1 the set C_n by removing from each of the 2^{n-1} closed interval components of C_{n-1} its symmetric open middle subinterval of length alpha_n, and let C = intersection_{n>=0} C_n. Find a recursive set-theoretic (nested) descriptive formula for the resulting deterministic Cantor set C subset of [0,1].
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's open problem on variable-gap deletions, not at Theorem 3.3 itself. The nearby context shows that the paper studies deterministic Cantor sets on the real line, uses nested representations as its basic recursive set-theoretic language, and presents the fixed-gap middle-alpha construction as the template case where a recursive description is already available. That makes the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite a stage-by-stage symmetric middle-deletion problem on [0,1] with a nested limit-set formulation. I did not add asymmetry, irrational endpoints, or other variants because the paper lists those as separate open directions, and I did not give an alternate formulation because the paper does not explicitly state an equivalence for this variable-gap problem itself.
